transcript.content: Hello, what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just... I keep getting hit out of nowhere with the scene of my cousin on that pavement. It's like I can hear the shouting and see the lights all over again. It happens even when I'm just standing in the church office trying to act normal, and I just don't know how to stop it.
How long ago did your cousin’s accident happen?
He was killed two years and three months ago. So... yeah, this has been going on ever since then.
Since your cousin’s death, have you deliberately avoided people, places, conversations, or activities that remind you of the accident?

Yeah, I do. I actually take the long way around town now just so I don't have to pass the community center or that court. And... if somebody starts talking about that night, I just shut it down right away. Or I'll find a reason to leave the room. I just can't be around anything that brings it up.
Since your cousin’s death, have you gotten into fights or acted aggressively in ways that caused problems?

Yeah, I have. Not physical fights, but... I've been snapping in ministry meetings over really small things. I'll just raise my voice at the deacons or the youth leaders, almost treating them like they're the enemy. And then afterward... I just hate how fast I went there. It's definitely causing some tension at the church.
Since the accident, have you often felt on guard or watchful, as if danger could happen at any moment?

Yeah, constantly. I actually can't sit with my back to a door anymore. And... at church events, instead of paying attention to the people right in front of me, I'm just always watching. I'm looking at people's hands, checking the corners of the room, watching cars slow down outside... and I always have to know exactly where the nearest exit is. I just can't seem to turn it off.
Have these symptoms been present continuously since the accident, without a sustained period when they went away?
Yeah, they have. There hasn't really been a break from it at all. This has just... it's been going on continuously since my cousin was killed two years and three months ago.
Since the accident, have you often felt detached or cut off from other people?

Yeah, I have. It's... it's a strange feeling. Even when I'm surrounded by people at church, you know, they're calling me 'brother' and asking me to pray with them... I just feel like I'm behind glass. Like they're there, but nobody can really reach me. I'm just completely cut off from them.

final_diagnosis.reason: Persistent posttraumatic symptoms for over two years following the accidental death of a cousin, including intrusive recollections, avoidance, detachment, hypervigilance, and irritability with church-related functional impairment, support chronic posttraumatic stress disorder.

confirmed_symptoms: Recurrent involuntary visual and auditory recollections of the cousin's death, including seeing the scene and hearing the shouting
Takes alternate routes to avoid locations associated with the accident
Avoids conversations about the accident and leaves situations when it is discussed
Feels detached and cut off from other people, describing the experience as being behind glass
Irritability and angry verbal outbursts during ministry meetings
Persistent hypervigilance, including monitoring exits, hands, room corners, and passing cars

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms have been continuously present for two years and three months since the cousin's death, without a sustained remission.
additional_requirements: Exposure to the accidental death of a family member was confirmed
Symptoms span intrusion, avoidance, negative interpersonal connection, and arousal/reactivity domains
Clinically significant impairment in church/ministry relationships was confirmed
